parts.problem_md:
This table shows the ages of 20 cars.

| Age (years) | Frequency |
|---|---|
| 1 | 2 |
| 2 | 7 |
| 3 | 4 |
| 4 | 3 |
| 5 | 4 |

Work out the range.

........................................ years
parts.solution_md:
> *Subtract the lowest age (1) from the greatest age (5)*

*5-1*

**4 ****[1]**

> *Multiply each age by its frequency*

| Age (years) | Frequency | Age $\times$ frequency |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 2 | $1\times2=2$ |
| 2 | 7 | $2\times7=14$ |
| 3 | 4 | $3\times4=12$ |
| 4 | 3 | $4\times3=12$ |
| 5 | 4 | $5\times4=20$ |

> *Add together the results*

> *This gives us the total of all our data added together*

$2+14+12+12+20=60$

**[1]**

> *Divide by how many pieces of data there are, 20*
*Be careful to avoid the common mistake here which would be to divide by the total number of rows *

$60\div20$

**[1]**

**3** **[1]**

parts.problem_md:
Five numbers have a mean of 9.4 . 
Four of the numbers are 3, 5, 10 and 12.

Work out the range of the five numbers.
parts.solution_md:
> *Multiply the mean by the number of data values to determine the sum of the values*

$9.4\times5=47$

**[1]**

> *Subtract the known values from the sum to determine the missing value*

$47 - ( 3 + 5 + 10 + 12 ) = 17$

**[1]**

> *The range is the difference between the highest and the lowest data values*

$17-3=14$

**[1]**

$14$ **[1]**

parts.problem_md:
The mean of three numbers is 150.

The numbers are 361, 2$n$ and $( n - 1 )$ .

Find the value of $n$.

$n$ = ...................................................
parts.solution_md:
> *Work out the total of the three numbers*

$150\times3=450$

> *The sum of the numbers must be equal to 450 so form an equation*

$361 + 2 n + ( n - 1 ) = 450$

**for 361 + 2n + n - 1**** [1] **
**correct equation ****[1]**

> *Collect like terms*

$360+3n=450$

> *Subtract 360 from both sides*

$3n=90$

> *Divide by 3*

$n=30$

**n**** = 30** **[1]**

**Extract:**

82 | 94 | 78 | 103 | 88 | 82

Another student, Toni, also brings an apple to school.

The mean mass of the 7 apples is 89g.

Work out the mass of Toni’s apple.

.............................................. g
parts.solution_md:
> *Add together the 7 numbers, including Toni's apple, to work out the total weight*

*78 + 82 + 82 + 88 + 94 + 103 + *$x$* = 527 + *$x$

**[1]**

> *Mean (89) = total (527 + *$x$*) *$\div$* how many pieces of data (7)*

$89 = ( 527 + x ) \div 7$

> * Multiply both sides of the equation by 7*

$\begin{gathered} 89 \times 7 & = 527 + x \\ \\ 623 = 527 + x \end{gathered}$

**[1]**

> *Subtract 527 from both sides*

$\begin{gathered} 623 - 527 & = x \\ \\ 96 = x \end{gathered}$

**96 g** **[1]**

parts.problem_md:
The mean of seven numbers is 16.

Six of these numbers are 12, 20, 19, 10, 21 and 13.

Find the seventh number.
parts.solution_md:
> *Multiply the mean (16) by 7 (the number of values) to find the total of all the values*

$16\times7=112$

**[1]**

> *Add up the numbers we already know*

$12+20+19+10+21+13=95$

> *Subtract 95 from the total, 112*

$112-95=17$

$17$ **[1]**

parts.problem_md:
The students in Class A and in Class B take the same examination.

The lowest score in Class A is 39 
The range of scores for Class A is 57 
The lowest score in Class B is 33 
The range of scores for Class B is 60

Find the range of scores for all the students in both classes.
parts.solution_md:
*Find the lowest overall score in both classes (the smaller of the two lowest class scores)*

*lowest overall score is 33*

*The range is the difference between the highest and lowest values* *Find the highest score in Class A (by adding its range to its lowest score)*

*highest score in Class A = 39 + 57 = 96*

*Find the highest score in Class B (by adding its range to its lowest score)*

*highest score in Class B = 33 + 60 = 93*

**either class highest score correct**** [1]**

*Find the highest overall score in both classes (the larger of the two highest class scores)* *  *

*highest overall score is 96*

*Find the overall range (the highest overall score subtract the lowest overall score)*

*overall range = 96 - 33*

**subtracting 33 from your highest score**** [1]**

**63 ****[1]**

> *Method 1: Using GDC*

> *Open a new spreadsheet/table on your calculator*

> *If possible on your calculator, turn off the frequency option in stats mode*

> *Enter each score into the first (data) column and leave the frequencies as 1 in the second column if it is required*

> *Open the statistics function, you may need to choose 'one variable statistics' and choose the option for:*

> *the range,  R*

**7 ****[1]**

> *the mode,  Mod*

**21 ****[1]**

> *the median,  Med*

**22.5 ****[1]**

> *the mean,  *$μ$

$22.71428571...$

**22.7 (3 s.f.) ****[1]**

> *Method 2*

> *The **range **is the difference between the maximum and minimum values.*

$27-20=7$

**Range = 7 ****[1]**

> *The **mode **is the number which occurs the most frequently.*

*21 (it appears 5 times)*

**Mode = 21 ****[1]**

> *The **median **is found by putting the numbers in order, and then finding the number in the middle. *
*As there are 14 pieces of data, the middle of the data set will be halfway between the 7*<sup>*th*</sup>* and 8*<sup>*th*</sup>* pieces of data. *
*If it isn't easy to spot, find the value halfway between two numbers by adding them together and dividing by 2. *
*You could also find the middle of the data by crossing out the numbers from each end alternately.*

$\cancel{20} \cancel{21} \cancel{21} \cancel{21} \cancel{21} \cancel{21} 22 23 \cancel{23} \cancel{23} \cancel{24} \cancel{25} \cancel{26} \cancel{27}$

*Halfway between 22 and 23 will be 22.5, which is the median*

**Median = 22.5 ****[1]**

> *To find the **mean**, find the sum of the data, and divide by how many pieces of data there are.*

$\frac{20+21+21+21+21+21+22+23+23+23+24+25+26+27}{14}$

$\frac{318}{14}=22.71428571...$

**Mean = 22.7 (3 s.f.) ****[1]**

parts.problem_md:
Roberto records the value of each of the coins he has at home. The table shows the results.

| Value (cents) | 1 | 2 | 5 | 10 | 20 | 50 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Frequency | 3 | 1 | 3 | 2 | 4 | 2 |

i) Find the range.

........................................... cents [1]

ii) Find the mode.

........................................... cents [1]

iii) Find the median.

........................................... cents [1]

iv) Work out the total value of Roberto’s coins.

........................................... cents [1]

v) Work out the mean.

........................................... cents [1]
parts.solution_md:
> *Method 1: Using GDC*

> *Open a new spreadsheet/table on your calculator*

> *Enter the Value row into the first (data) column (label this V) and the frequencies into the second column (label this f)*

> *Open the statistics function, you may need to choose 'one variable statistics' and choose the option for:*

i)* the range,  R*

**49 cents ****[1]**

ii)* the mode,  Mod*

**20 cents ****[1]**

iii)* the median,  Med*

**10 cents ****[1]**

iv)* the sum of values,  *$Σx$

**220 cents ****[1]**

v)* the mean,  *$μ$* or *$\overline{x}$

$14.66666...$

**14.7 cents ****[1]**
**An answer between 14.66 to 14.67 will be accepted**

> *Method 2*

i) *Subtract the lowest value coin from the highest value coin to find the range.*

$50-1$

**49 cents ****[1]**

ii) *The mode is the most common number, so identify the type of coin with the highest frequency.*

**20 cents** **[1]**

iii) *The median is the middle value. It's position can be found using *$\frac{n+1}{2}$*.*

> *Find the total number of coins (*$n$*) by adding together the frequencies of the different types.*

$3+1+3+2+4+2=15$

> *Add one to the total and then divide by 2.*

$( 15 + 1 ) \div 2 = 8$

> *Starting from the lowest value coin, find the value of the 8*<sup>*th*</sup>* coin.*

*The 8**<sup>th</sup>** coin lies in the 10 cents column*

**10 cents** **[1]**

iv) *Multiply the value of each coin by how many there are of that type.*

$( 1 \times 3 ) + ( 2 \times 1 ) + ( 5 \times 3 ) + ( 10 \times 2 ) + ( 20 \times 4 ) + ( 50 \times 2 )$

**220 cents** **[1]**

v) *Divide the total value of the coins by how many coins there are.*

$\frac{220}{15}=14.66666...$

**Final answer:** **14.7 cents**** [1]**

**An answer between 14.66 to 14.67 will be accepted.**
